\subsection{Fresh clone-controlled evidence on MATH-500 (WP-1R/WP-2R)}
\label{sec:wp1r}

The archived studies lack matched repeats and a same-code control, so they
cannot separate stable complementarity from one-run sampling luck. A fresh
pre-registered collection (frozen 2026-09-15; Appendix~\ref{app:wp1r})
executes a frozen eight-harness panel plus \bare{} on the 400 MATH-500
eval tasks for three independent repeats, plus nine equal-budget
same-code \bare{} clone slots --- the repeated-sampling baseline of
\S\ref{related:diversity}.

C-rank is \textsc{\WpCrankState}; C-comp is \textsc{\WpCcompState}.
The frozen A8.6 procedure selects the best member on repeat 1 and scores
its held-out advantage over \bare{} on repeats 2--3: $\WpAReal$\,pp (real)
versus $\WpAClone$\,pp (clones), paired $D=\WpADiff$\,pp on
\WpANtasksPaired{} shared complete tasks (95\% CI $\WpADiffCI$;
$p=\WpAPerm$); both sensitivity branches agree ($D=\WpImputedD$ and
$\WpConflictD$\,pp). The frozen coverage gate makes the verdict
\textsc{\WpAState}: no advantage over equal-budget same-code sampling.
The acquisition consumed \WpLogicalCalls{} logical calls (\WpCostCny{}
CNY ceiling) and is hash-sealed.

\paragraph{Selector utility (E3).} The frozen pre-execution policy
$\pi_Z$ abstains to \bare{} on every eval task (no member clears the
frozen 0.15 confidence margin) and so ties both dev-fixed and \bare{} at
\WpBareAcc\%; it realizes no selection gain (paired
$\WpPiZDiff$\,pp, CI $\WpPiZDiffCI$), while a pre-fixed random member is
materially worse ($\WpRandomDiff$\,pp, CI $\WpRandomCI$;
Table~\ref{tab:wp1r-policy}). Class D
therefore yields no evidence of usable pre-execution selectability on
this panel, and the $b{=}3$ budgeted utility $U_b$ (Class E) is
\WpEbZero{}-gain for all frozen policies.
